findings.issue_summary: Data Safety Compliant (Local-Only): No account identifier is collected or transmitted; the 'uid' matches are substring false positives inside localized UI strings.
findings.evidence: Semantic grounding rejects both hits. app/src/main/res/values-es/strings.xml:149 <string name="sw_meldung_sprache_wird_geladen">...Intentalo de nuevo enseguida.</string> - the pattern 'uid' is the literal substring of the Spanish word 'enseguida'; it is display copy about a language pack download, not an account ID. simple-keyboard/src/main/res/values-nl/strings.xml:23 <string name="sound_on_keypress">Geluid bij toetsaanslag</string> (also lines 42, 51) - 'uid' is a substring of the Dutch word 'Geluid' (sound), a keypress-sound preference label. Neither is an account ID, account number, or account name. Corroborating architectural evidence: the shipping app declares no network egress at all. app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:4-9 carries the explicit comment 'Kein INTERNET-Recht: Nibra erkennt ausschliesslich auf dem Geraet' and requests only android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO; grep for android.permission.INTERNET across all non-build AndroidManifest.xml files returns exactly one hit, app/src/forschung/AndroidManifest.xml:13, which belongs to the 'forschung' research flavor that its own header documents as 'ausdruecklich **kein** Auslieferungsstand: eigener Paketname ... und sie gehoert nie in einen Laden'. app/build.gradle.kts:114-143 and simple-keyboard/build.gradle.kts:26-27 list only AndroidX/Compose/Hilt/Room/DataStore/coroutines and preference/appcompat; gradle/libs.versions.toml contains no match for firebase, crashlytics, analytics, retrofit, okhttp, ktor, adjust, appsflyer, mixpanel, or ads. No HTTP client, WebView, or telemetry SDK exists in the release source set.
findings.recommendation: No action required. Do not declare USER_ACCOUNT in the Play Console Data Safety form on the basis of these matches - both are localization substrings. Keep the release flavor free of android.permission.INTERNET and ensure the 'forschung' flavor is never uploaded to Play, since it is the only build that can reach the network.
findings.purpose: Local functionality only (localized UI strings; no account data processed)

findings.issue_summary: Data Safety Compliant (Local-Only): No gender or other personal attribute is collected; the 'gender' match is a substring of a German test name in an excluded test source set.
findings.evidence: app/src/testForschung/java/de/ithandwerkstuttgart/nibra/forschung/MesswerkzeugTest.kt:523 fun `ein gleichmaessig steigender boden gilt als leck`() - the pattern 'gender' is the literal substring of the German participle 'steigender' (rising) in a backtick-quoted unit-test method name about a rising noise floor being treated as a leak. It carries no semantic relation to date of birth, gender identity, veteran status, or any other personal attribute. The file additionally lives in a unit-test source set (src/testForschung/) that ships no code into any APK and is inside the mandated exclusion scope for shipped-code analysis. No field, parameter, UI input, or persisted column for a personal attribute exists at or around this location, and the release app has no network sink to transmit one (app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml declares only RECORD_AUDIO, no INTERNET).
findings.recommendation: No action required; treat as a false positive from substring matching. Do not declare PERSONAL_INFO_OTHER in the Data Safety form on this basis.
findings.purpose: Local functionality only (unit test naming; no personal attribute processed)

findings.issue_summary: Data Safety Compliant (Local-Only): getPackageInfo queries only the app's own package for its version name/code; no inventory of installed apps is built or transmitted.
findings.evidence: simple-keyboard/src/main/java/rkr/simplekeyboard/inputmethod/latin/utils/ApplicationUtils.java:58-59 (getVersionName) and :76-77 (getVersionCode) both read 'final String packageName = context.getPackageName();' immediately followed by 'final PackageInfo info = context.getPackageManager().getPackageInfo(packageName, 0);'. The package name is the caller's own, obtained from its own Context - this is a self-version lookup, not an enumeration of third-party apps. The methods return only info.versionName (String) and info.versionCode (int); no PackageInfo of any other app is retrieved, and the class contains no getInstalledPackages, getInstalledApplications, or queryIntentActivities call. Scope confirmation: no AndroidManifest.xml in the project declares android.permission.QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES (grep across all non-build manifests returns no hit). app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:25-29 declares a single narrow <queries> block for the intent action android.speech.RecognitionService, documented in the manifest comment as required so the on-device recognizer is visible at all ('AppsFilter: nibra -> com.google.android.as BLOCKED'); this grants visibility of the speech service only and no app list leaves the device. Sink analysis: the release app has no network capability (only RECORD_AUDIO in app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:9), and gradle/libs.versions.toml declares no analytics, crash-reporting, or HTTP library, so these version values reach no off-device sink.
findings.recommendation: No action required. Retain the narrow <queries> intent filter rather than QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES, and do not declare APPS_ON_DEVICE in the Data Safety form. If a future build adds crash reporting, re-check that the version string is not paired with an app inventory.
findings.purpose: Local functionality only (own app version lookup for settings display)

findings.issue_summary: Data Safety Compliant (Local-Only): The keyboard only classifies an EditText's inputType variation as an e-mail field; no e-mail address value is read, stored, or transmitted.
findings.evidence: simple-keyboard/src/main/java/rkr/simplekeyboard/inputmethod/latin/utils/InputTypeUtils.java:57-59 'private static boolean isWebEmailAddressVariation(int variation) { return variation == TYPE_TEXT_VARIATION_WEB_EMAIL_ADDRESS; }' and :61-64 'public static boolean isEmailVariation(final int variation) { return variation == TYPE_TEXT_VARIATION_EMAIL_ADDRESS || isWebEmailAddressVariation(variation); }'. Both operate purely on the integer inputType/variation bitmask supplied by the Android framework in EditorInfo; they take an int and return a boolean. No String containing an address is read, no CharSequence is captured, and the surrounding class (isTextPasswordInputType, isPasswordInputType at :53-70) is a pure classification helper used to decide keyboard behaviour such as suppressing suggestions on password and e-mail fields - a privacy-protective use, the opposite of collection. Semantic grounding therefore fails to connect this to 'a user's email address'. Sink analysis: no manifest in the project grants android.permission.GET_ACCOUNTS (grep over all non-build manifests returns no hit), so no account e-mail can be enumerated either. The release app declares no INTERNET permission (app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:9 lists only RECORD_AUDIO), and no HTTP/telemetry dependency exists in app/build.gradle.kts:114-143, simple-keyboard/build.gradle.kts:26-27, or gradle/libs.versions.toml - so even if a value were captured there is no off-device sink to receive it.
findings.recommendation: No action required; do not declare EMAIL in the Data Safety form on this basis. Keep using isEmailVariation to suppress learning/suggestions on sensitive fields, and re-audit only if a future change starts persisting the composing text of e-mail-typed fields.
findings.purpose: Local functionality only (input-type classification to adjust keyboard behaviour)

findings.issue_summary: Data Safety Compliant (Local-Only): 'display_name' refers to keyboard layout display labels from a static string array, not to a user's name.
findings.evidence: simple-keyboard/src/main/java/rkr/simplekeyboard/inputmethod/latin/utils/SubtypeLocaleUtils.java:602-604 'final String[] predefinedLayoutDisplayNames = mResources.getStringArray(R.array.predefined_layout_display_names); layoutNameStr = predefinedLayoutDisplayNames[predefinedLayoutIndex];' and the identical pattern at :639-640. The value is read from a static app resource array (R.array.predefined_layout_display_names) indexed by the keyboard layout id resolved at :597-599 from R.array.predefined_layouts, and is then passed at :609-610 into 'new Subtype(mLocale, keyboardLayoutSet, layoutNameStr, false, mResources)' - a keyboard-layout descriptor used to label entries in the language/layout picker (e.g. QWERTY, AZERTY). It is developer-authored resource text, never user input, and semantic grounding rules it out as 'how a user refers to themselves, such as their first or last name, or nickname'. This is a canonical false positive of the fileName/display_name kind. Sink analysis: the release app has no network egress - app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:4-9 documents 'Kein INTERNET-Recht' and requests only RECORD_AUDIO, the single INTERNET declaration in the repository is confined to the non-shippable research flavor at app/src/forschung/AndroidManifest.xml:13, and no analytics, crash-reporting, or HTTP dependency appears in gradle/libs.versions.toml.
findings.recommendation: No action required; do not declare NAME in the Data Safety form on this basis. The value is a static layout label with no user identity content.
findings.purpose: Local functionality only (keyboard layout labels in the settings picker)
